sec: BCS presentation, prognosis, mechanism flowchart, investigations and management

items.q: Most common presentation demographic of BCS printed?
Fill up: Ascites in BCS arises from zone ______ involvement → sinusoidal ______ + pooling.
items.exp: 'Ascites : zone 3 involvement → sinusoidal distension + pooling.' (Book p1034)

items.q: Subacute BCS — judge: I It is the most common presentation. II It causes refractory ascites with collaterals. III The ascites is high-SAAG, high-protein.
opts: I and II true, III false
II and III true, I false
I true, II and III false
items.exp: '1. Subacute : m/c presentation; Refractory ascites + collaterals; High SAAG, high protein ascites.' (Book p1034)

items.q: A patient's ascitic fluid shows high SAAG and LOW protein. Per the Note on this page, what does this pattern indicate?
opts: Post-sinusoidal (hepatic venous) cause such as BCS
items.exp: 'Note : High SAAG, low protein ascites : Sinusoidal cause.' (BCS gives high SAAG, high protein.) (Book p1034)

items.q: Acute hepatitis presentation of BCS: what jaundice frequency is printed and how common is fulminant hepatic failure?
opts: Jaundice universal; fulminant hepatic failure rare
items.exp: '2. Acute Hepatitis : Abdominal pain + hepatomegaly + ascites; Jaundice : <10% patients; Fulminant hepatic failure : Rare.' Then '3. Cirrhosis'. (Book p1034)

items.q: Mechanism flowchart, LEFT column — put in order: A) Extravasation of fluid from hepatic vein > sinusoids B) Increased sinusoidal & portal pressure C) High SAAG, high protein ascites D) Sinusoidal distension
items.exp: Hepatic venous outflow obstruction → Increased sinusoidal & portal pressure → Sinusoidal distension → Extravasation of fluid from hepatic vein > sinusoids → High SAAG, high protein ascites. (Book p1034)

items.q: Mechanism flowchart, RIGHT column — put in order: A) Fibrosis, nodular regenerative hyperplasia B) Venous stasis and congestion C) Hepatocyte necrosis (centrilobular) leading to lobar collapse D) Hypoxic damage to hepatocytes, zone 3 involvement
items.exp: Venous stasis and congestion → Hypoxic damage to hepatocytes, zone 3 → Hepatocyte necrosis (centrilobular) leading to lobar collapse → Fibrosis, nodular regenerative hyperplasia → Cirrhosis. Caption: 'mechanism of Ascites & Cirrhosis in BCS'. (Book p1034)

items.q: Investigations — match — 1) Hepatic venous Doppler 2) CECT 3) MRI … A) IOC B) Nodules / hemorrhagic liver C) Screening test; obstruction + portosystemic collaterals
items.exp: Doppler: screening test, obstruction + portosystemic collaterals; CECT: IOC; MRI: nodules/hemorrhagic liver. (Book p1034)

items.q: What does the red arrow on the 'CECT image in BCS' point to?
items.exp: Label: 'Caudate lobe hypertrophy' — CECT image in BCS. (Book p1034)

items.q: Management of BCS: which statement matches the printed text?
opts: Anticoagulation is mandatory for all; non-decompensated patients get angioplasty ± stenting, and on failure TIPSS
Anticoagulation only if PNH; all others go straight to TIPSS
Angioplasty is reserved for decompensated patients; anticoagulation is optional
Liver transplant is first-line in all non-decompensated patients
items.exp: 'mandatory anticoagulation to all. Non decompensated patients : Angioplasty +/− stenting —Failure→ TIPSS (Transjugular Intrahepatic Porto-systemic Shunt).' (Book p1034)
